content.contents: nobody... nobody likes me? what? where did that come from?

alright so, maybe i have a lot of self doubt and even a tinge of self hatred here and there, but no, i don't really believe nobody likes me. i have juuuust enough self confidence to be able to name an album something so ridiculous. of course, ironic humor is something i love, so, the irony of calling an album that's purely a compilation of remixes made by people i'm friends with is nowhere near lost on me. in fact, it's the entire point!

the text on the front was written by myself! sxnctuary, drexgod, dead fave and simvlacrvm don't actually think those things, and never messaged me such vulgar displays of vitriol. it's kind of a weird album cover though, no? i can't take the credit for making it myself. it's inspired by...
this album cover! from none other than one of my biggest inspirations for piano plyaing, Bill Evans!

i found myself listening to this album quite a bit last year, and looking at the cover as much as i did sorta made me think how funny it would be to write the polar opposite for a cover. as such, NOBODY LIKES STATIC.GRL was born.

i wanted to do a nice little homage to bill evans because i love him so much. at first it was going to be a little EP with remixes from a couple friends, i kind of figured it could be just 4 people so that each of their signatures could be placed on the cover. but then i thought, well, i've made a lot of friends through collaborations nad hanging out amidst the scene. and THEN i thought, shit, no way cna i rope such an amount of people into remixing one of my tracks. so i messaged simvlacrvm for a confidence boost (happens more often than you'd think), and he said, why not just ask? there's no harm in asking. i guess a part of me just thought, i don't know, maybe i'd seem kind of self-centred and narcissistic if i asked everyone to remix *my* work. but actually, who cares? all i would pose is a question, do you want to remix a track of mine? and in that statement alone i ended up finding a group of 13 different folks who agreed to it. after organizing the group in question i had another thought...
what if we sold it phsyically, and then donated all the proceeds to charity?

i mean, right from the get-go i knew i wanted to use trans colors for the cover. in fact, i thought it would fit perfectly from a design perspective, and... i mean, i think i was right! i hope! lol
but then, last year just sucked for trans people. it was just awful, especially in the states and the UK, so all i could think about was how badly i wished to give back to that same community that had given me so much love, and more importantly, had taught me how to love myself. so, i proceeded to contact all who had helped me by remixing tracks and to my elation, everybody agreed! undeniable, unequivocal proof that this community kicks fucking ass.

i want you all to know, though, how fukcing long this album took to make. according to file dates, the first iteration of the album cover was created July last year. initially, my plan was to release it not long after GUYAG, which was at the time slated for release in September. i was thinking of releasing it as a christmas bonus album of sorts, but of course after GUYAG's two delays that fell through. i was also in contact with another label regarding getting a very limited vinyl press going, as well as a CD run, but that fell through, so i instead took it upon myself to push the thing out, and i'm pleased to say thus far it's been a fantastic success! as of writing, we've raised $350USD for Mermaids UK, and sales seem to be flowing steady! hopefully it continues to sell OK so we can continue to raise funds, but i'm honestly blown away by the reception thus far. to be able to raise any amount for my people is honestly an honor. a completely honor.

i'd also like to once again thank everyone who helped make this project a reality! everyone was so patient and diligent waiting for their tracks to be posted, and the fact that they all agreed to donate their shares of the sales to charity alongside me gives me faith that hey, maybe shit ain't so bad.
if you'd like to purchase the album on CD, you can do so [https://kunaki.com/msales.ASP?Publisherid=239310&PP=1](here!)
and if you'd like to purchase a bandcamp copy, you can do so [https://staticgrl.bandcamp.com/album/nobody-likes-static-grl-52656d697865732c20766f6c2e2031](here!!!)
now, i'd also like to talk a bit about my personal life as of late, because a lot has happened, so if you'll indulge me...

well, where to start? i've moved recently to Plymouth. if you live in the area, come say hi, i'll be working in Sappho's most days doing freelance stuff on my laptop. feels better to be in a city, especially one with quite a few queers around, it's been hopelessly depressing living as long as i have in such a transphobic and mean-spirited right-wing area. i'm not far from family here either which is wonderful. unfortunately, this move has resulted in me parting ways with my girlfriend. i won't share all the juicy details because, to be honest, there's a distinct lack thereof. it was really amicable. we still love each other a lot. it just wasn't working, mainly because i lived in such a horrific part of England. so, here we are, i feel like i've turned over another proverbial page in static's book of life, and it's nice but also incredibly fucking daunting. it's been a while since i've been truly independent, so to be put into that position again - rather, to put myself in that position myself, it feels like quite a challenge. but, a healthy challenge! i think i really need to push myself a little bit, i need to come out of my shell. things were too, i don't know, easy, convenient, and i was relaly really lonely. had everything i thought i ever wanted, besides community, and i guess i didn't really understand how important community was to me. but now, as i sit and write this blog in a queer cafe surrounded by fellow gays, i can't help but think... this is what i've needed. this is what i've wanted, what i've been striving for for years. to have it practically on my doorstep, i mean, i feel blessed.

to be quite honest, i've not been a massive fan of plymouth historically. considering i was raised in and around Cornwall, i already had a fair amount of knowledge of the city, it was really the closest city to me. so it was like, if you wanted to actually do something fun like go see a movie or get some decent food you'd have to take the bus to plymouth. and back when i was younger it felt like a real rough shithole, but in recent years it seems (to me, at least) that the culture around here has improved exponentially. even today, as i walked to get some errands done in the central area i saw the council had put out a trans flag on their central pole for trans day of visibility. lord knows that wouldn't happen where i lived prior! and if it did it'd be slandered to all hell across the local media. there's be protests against it. feels good. i understand there's still a lot of assholes around but at the same time, there's a lot more people who are chill with people, y'know, being.

in my (albeit extremely limitied) experience thus far, i get stared at much less than i did back north. older folks tend to look once then look away. maybe it's like exposure therapy? they've seen more of us around so there's less fear, bewilderment? i don't know, i guess i don't really care either. the point is, i don't have to feel so terribly self conscious as i did. and sure, it's been easy for a long time to sit and say, why do you give a fuck what others think? but if you were glared at as much as i have been, you'd start to feel the same. just, purely unwelcome. it's like the act of existence becomes a chore, one that wasn't getting any easier where i was at. all in all, this feels like the right step. or at the very least, the next step.
anyway, i've got shit to do, music to write, coffee to drink, and uh... i don't know, some one-liner that makes you chuckle. so i'm gonna go! thanks for reading, i love you all<3
